settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: Within Shiro both the path used for pattern matching (PathMatchingFilter preHandle, lines 172-183) and the chain selection (PathMatchingFilterChainResolver.getChain, lines 99-116) use the same normalized value, so a purely internal mismatch is not evident.
decodeAndCleanUriString strips the ';' segment (line 233-234) and normalize collapses '//' and '/./','/../' (lines 188-216), which removes several common bypass primitives.
The servlet container typically performs its own canonicalization before Shiro sees request.getRequestURI(), and Shiro relies on the container-resolved URI by design.
candidates.description: WebUtils.getPathWithinApplication() computes the value used both by PathMatchingFilter.preHandle() and PathMatchingFilterChainResolver.getChain() to decide which configured URL patterns apply, and therefore which authentication/authorization filters run. The path is produced by getRequestUri() -> normalize(decodeAndCleanUriString(request, uri)). decodeAndCleanUriString() applies URLDecoder.decode once and truncates at the first ';' (line 233-234). normalize() replaces backslashes with '/', collapses '//', resolves '/./' and '/../' (lines 178-216). This is a single decode plus a hand-rolled normalization. It does not reject encoded separators that survive one decode, repeated/over-encoded traversal (%252e%252e, %2f, %5c depending on the container's own decoding), or NUL/other control bytes. The class Javadoc itself warns that normalize 'does not try to perform security checks for malicious input' (lines 145-147, 160-162). If any servlet container or downstream framework resolves the concrete request target differently from this normalized string, a request could match a permissive pattern in Shiro (e.g. a pattern intended to be public) while being routed to a protected resource, or vice-versa. This is reported as an unresolved candidate: within Shiro's own code the matched path and the matched pattern derive from the same normalized value, so no in-code bypass was demonstrated.
missing_evidence: No concrete container (Tomcat/Jetty/Undertow) request-and-normalization test demonstrating a pattern that Shiro matches to a public chain while the container routes the request to a protected resource.
No analysis of how encoded backslash/slash or double-encoded traversal behaves end-to-end through WebUtils.decodeRequestString and the container.
No application URL-pattern configuration showing a permissive pattern that an attacker-controlled URI could be matched against.
preconditions: Shiro web filter chain active, with URL-pattern-based filter chains (authc/authz filters bound to Ant-style patterns).

Deployed behind a servlet container whose request-target normalization/decoding differs from Shiro's single-decode + normalize logic (e.g. differing treatment of encoded slashes/backslashes, double-encoding, or ';' path parameters).
A configuration where the differing normalization lets a request match a less-protective pattern than the one governing the actual routed resource.
candidates.title: Request-URI normalization in WebUtils may be insufficient to prevent path-pattern (filter-chain) matching discrepancies
